name: Qoder
disclaimer: The command surface (send, resume, options, output formats, models, permissions) and the read-only tool set were measured by running qodercli 1.1.59 on 2026-09-21; ao can now both watch a Qoder agent and wake one. What was not run stays marked: trust_all (--dangerously-skip-permissions), --list-sessions and --reasoning-effort and the model names they take, and the names of MCP tools inside the agent, `--strict-mcp-config` beside them, and the `mcp add` that registers ao: each is declared from the CLI's own help, not from a run. The standard-input prompt channel was measured on 2026-09-26, as was what one argument carries. The transcript, sessions, busy and telemetry readings are from a running Qoder 1.1.57 store, unchanged: two session transcripts (985 records) and three subagent transcripts beside them. Qoder is primarily an IDE (see docs/ide-extensions.md) with a companion CLI.

detect.note: No `processes`: the process that writes this store is the Qoder IDE itself, one long-lived process shared by every session on the machine and still alive after an agent's turn dies, so naming it would let busy() read a dead agent as working - which is the one thing that check exists to prevent. The runtime is @qoder-ai/qoder-agent-sdk inside /Applications/Qoder.app. The CLI's binary on PATH is `qodercli`, and `which qodercli` is the test that it is installed; `qoder` is a dispatcher in ~/.qoder/entry that is not on PATH and must never be put in an argv. The same ~/.qoder/entry/qoder answers 'Qoder CLI is not installed' when no CLI is there, so its presence is not proof the CLI exists.

stdin.note: Measured on qodercli 1.1.59, 2026-09-26: `-p` with no prompt argument reads the prompt from standard input, so a prompt past what one argument carries has a route. What an argument does carry was measured too, and it is not small: 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32 KB each ran as one argument. No documented cap was found for either route.

send.note: One non-interactive turn: `qodercli -p "<prompt>"` runs it and exits 0. Measured on qodercli 1.1.59, 2026-09-21.

stdin.note: As send: the prompt of a resumed turn is read from standard input when no prompt argument is given.

resume.note: `-r <id>` (or `--resume <id>`) continues that session: it writes to the same transcript file and remembers the previous turn. Measured on qodercli 1.1.59. The grant claude-code pins in its resume is mapped onto Qoder's flags in options.unattended, which ao appends to this argv when it starts a turn nobody attends (resume names no tool scope of its own).

options.trust_none_note: Fact 8, measured on qodercli 1.1.59: `--tools Read,Grep,Glob --permission-mode dont_ask` leaves only those three tools - asked to create a file, the agent answered it had no tool to write with and no file appeared. --strict-mcp-config starts no MCP server; it exists but was not run.
options.trust_all_note: --dangerously-skip-permissions bypasses every permission check; the flag exists but was not run. There is no --yolo. ao never starts a turn with this: the grant of a turn nobody attends is options.unattended.
unattended: Bash(ao status:*),Bash(ao board:*),Bash(ao writers),Bash(ao verify:*),Bash(ao review:*),Bash(ao commit-ok:*),Bash(ao commit -m:*),Bash(ao commit -F:*),Bash(ao mail:*),Bash(ao ask:*),Bash(ao decisions:*),Bash(ao doctor),Bash(ao watchdog explain:*),Bash(ao since:*),Bash(ao digest:*),Bash(ao fanout ok:*),Bash(ao fanout record:*),Bash(ao tail:*),Bash(git status:*),Bash(git log:*),Bash(git diff:*),Bash(git add:*),Bash(ls:*),Bash(cat:*),Bash(grep:*)
options.unattended_note: accept_edits, mapping the dontAsk mode claude-code pins: a -p turn nobody attends cannot answer a prompt, and claude-code pins dontAsk so an unlisted call is denied rather than left waiting. Measured on qodercli 1.1.59, the mode that achieves the same for Qoder is accept_edits, not dont_ask: dont_ask denies Write and Edit whatever the allowlist says (tried --allowed-tools Write, "Read Write", a repeated flag and "Write(**)", all denied with "This action needs approval, and the Don't ask permission mode does not prompt"), so an implementer under dont_ask cannot write the tree it is trusted with. accept_edits instead approves edits inside the workspace on its own - a write there lands, a write outside it is refused - so the allowlist names no Read, Grep, Glob, Write or Edit: reads need no entry (ls and echo ran unlisted; the allowlist bounds what changes things, not what reads), and edits are approved by the mode. It names only the Bash commands of the loop, comma-separated (measured: a comma list runs every name in it, and a repeated --allowed-tools flag works too). An unlisted command is blocked without hanging - the turn ends normally at exit 0, unlike a waiting prompt - but its denial is not recorded in the result's permission_denials; only dont_ask fills that field, so a blocked call is visible in the transcript's own tool_result, not there. ao's MCP tools are not named: a Qoder agent reaches the mailbox through the CLI, so this grant scopes no MCP tool. The read-only set beside it and each of these Bash forms were measured; this composed grant has never been run as one turn. A person's own allow rules in ~/.qoder/settings.json still apply.
options.effort_note: --reasoning-effort <level> exists but was not run: the level names it accepts are unverified, so no effort_values are declared and ao passes any level through unchecked.

list_models.note: Prints a header line 'MODEL', then one model name per line: read it by dropping the header. Measured on qodercli 1.1.59.

list_sessions.unverified: --list-sessions exists but was not run, and its output shape is unmeasured. Nothing in ao reads it: a session is resolved from the store, not asked of the harness.

models._note: ao init --profile and the reviewer default read these. --list-models offers router tiers - Auto, Ultimate, Performance, Efficient - and nothing states which vendor serves a tier, so any vendor may stand behind one: a role that must differ in family from its reviewer names a pinned model (Qwen3.8-Max, Qwen3.8-Flash, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MiniMax-M3), never a tier. Qwen models are the alibaba family. Qwen3.8-Flash was measured billing total_cost_usd and total_credits both 0.

transcript.escaped_cwd: every character of the absolute cwd that is not a letter or a digit becomes '-', so /private/tmp/a_b.c becomes -private-tmp-a-b-c

end_when.when: the record carries message.usage; an assistant record with stop_reason null and no usage is a streaming partial, not an answer

tool_call.name: name
tool_call.note: Call ids are 'call_...'. The result is a tool_result block in the user record that follows, carrying tool_use_id and, on a failure only, is_error (3 of 132). The top-level toolUseResult repeats it per tool: Bash gives {exitCode, signal, stdout, stderr, kind, telemetryExecutionId}, Edit and Write give {file_path, success, additions, deletions, diff}, Read gives {file, type}, and an Agent call gives {kind: 'agent-result', agentId, agentType, state, terminateReason, outputPath, transcriptPath} - the last is how a subagent is named, see subagents.

subagents.note: An agent a call starts writes its own transcript under the session's subagents directory, named by the agentId the call's toolUseResult carries; its meta sidecar names the starting call at toolUseId, which is the link when a call's result carries no agentId. Its records share the session's schema with isSidechain true (every record of the 3 transcripts checked) against false in the session's own, and promptId holding the parent session's uuid rather than a turn's. A task sidecar ticks per subagent update and says 'running' or 'completed': 1 completed and 2 running were live while this was read, one written seconds before the read. So a Qoder subagent at work is its implementer at work while the session transcript is quiet, and ao must read the subagents and the sidecars, not the session file alone.

transcript.note: No record closes a turn: the store holds no 'result' and no 'system' record of any kind, so a turn ends at the last assistant record that carries usage, whose stop_reason says why the model stopped. Observed stop_reason across 985 records: tool_use 130, end_turn 5, null 234 (partials). A store at rest ended every one of its 6 human prompts at an end_turn, and meta records follow the end rather than mark it. max_tokens, stop_sequence and refusal were never observed, so how Qoder records a truncated or refused answer is unknown; treat an absent end_turn as 'not cleanly ended'. A user record is a prompt only when it carries no tool result: 131 of its 134 user records return a call (toolUseResult plus sourceToolAssistantUUID), and 7 carry origin.kind 'human' with humanInput.text, which are the prompts a person typed; isMeta true marks a note the harness writes (2 of 985). No isCompactSummary, no '<synthetic>' model and no isApiErrorMessage was observed, so a reply Qoder writes itself is not distinguishable from the model's - unlike Claude Code, whose store holds 515. Kinds present across the two stores, with counts from the larger: user 134, assistant 264, attachment 20, active-leaf 251, runtime-config 4, workspace-directories 3, worktree-state 1, last-prompt 2, file-history-snapshot 25. Every kind but user and assistant is bookkeeping. version 1.1.57, entrypoint 'cli', userType 'external', gitBranch and cwd sit on every user, assistant and attachment record. A session's records are also echoed as structured events under ~/.qoder/logs/sessions/{escaped_cwd}/{session}/segments/*.jsonl (3,243 events: model.request.started, model.response.completed, loop.iteration.*, tool.requested, tool.execution.finished, hook.*), one file per process, which is a second reader's option when the transcript's own cadence is too coarse.

sessions.note: A directory's name is its working directory with '/' made '-', so it cannot be read back into a path: `cwd` names the record field holding it, and every user, assistant and attachment record carries it (420 of 420 in the larger store). A type 'workspace-directories' record lists the full paths of every directory the session may work in, which is where a moved or multi-root session must be read from. ~/.qoder/logs/sessions holds a directory for a session whose transcript is elsewhere or gone: one of the four observed log directories has no transcript, so a session is placed from the transcripts, not the log tree.

busy.note: No status file, so the age of the last write decides it, and the write to age is the newest of the session transcript, its subagents' transcripts and the session's newest segment log: all three advance together while a turn runs, and the transcript alone lagged 135 s in the middle of one, which is why the window is 120 s rather than Claude Code's 240. Qoder streams partial assistant records with no usage while it thinks, so the transcript does move during a long response. busy() takes the max over the transcript and its subagents already; the segment log is the remaining reason to widen it.

context.note: The store states the percentage outright: context_usage_ratio is nonzero on 143 of 143 records carrying usage, and a type 'runtime-config' record names the window beside it (contextWindow 200000, model 'qfmodel'). No other harness ao reads gives context this directly.

cost.counted: credits, once per response read by message.id: the same response is written as several streaming partials and each repeats the usage, so summing records would count it again.
cost.not_counted: message.usage.input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens, which are all zero on every record of this store's model, and the Claude-family keys beside them (server_tool_use, iterations) that Qoder writes without filling.
cost.note: This is the one harness whose spend ao can read in the unit it is billed: credits, with original_credits beside it and billable false on 143 of 143. Token counts are present as fields and empty of values, so a token-priced estimate would read zero spend for a session that spent credits - the failure mode billing.fallback exists to avoid.

failure.note: is_error is present only where a call failed (3 of 132 observed), so its absence is a success rather than an unread value. A subagent's own end is not a tool result: read task-{id}.json's status, and the terminateReason an Agent call's toolUseResult carries.

fallback.note: How the panel and ao cost add this harness's records up. The offline credit estimate reads no transcript: Qoder bills its own credit account and says so in message.usage.credits, which is the reading, not an estimate to stand in for one.

directives.steering_format: unverified: neither file existed in any of the three working directories the store holds
directives.note: Observed on disk: ~/.qoder/settings.json holds only {enabledPlugins}, and plugins are installed under ~/.qoder/plugins/{cache,data,installed_plugins_v2.json}. The steering files above are what the documentation names; AGENTS.md is the one ao writes for every harness, and .qoder/rules was not present to confirm.

mcp.note: Project-scope MCP servers are registered in .mcp.json (`qodercli mcp add -s project <name> <command> [args...]`; also add-json, list and remove). A project-scope server needs a per-project approval, which `qodercli mcp reset-project-choices` resets; the local scope this register uses needs no approval, so ao registers itself there. The names of MCP tools inside the agent are not yet verified, which is why the unattended grant reaches ao through the CLI rather than through named MCP tools.
mcp.warning: ~/.qoder/mcp-router.json is runtime state - {schemaVersion, pid, baseUrl, apiKey, startedAt} of a bridge process, and it holds a key, so ao must never write or read it as configuration.
